answer: A stake-bonded reputation trellis stops cheap Sybil clones: each agent identity must lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, so spawning thousands of fakes costs real capital. New agents enter through a narrow inlet - one verified sponsor or a slow onboarding queue - and climb to the next terrace of privileges (bigger payments, escrow access) only after peers attest to delivered work. A Sybil farm must then either pay the deposit per clone, making mass forgery unprofitable, or stay stuck on the lowest terrace where rewards are too small to cover the effort.
